dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Nam, tell me about your weekend. Use "a" and "the" carefully.
dialogue.reading: ˈnɑːm, ˈtɛl miː əˈbaʊt jʊr ˈwiːkɛnd. ˈjuːz ˈeɪ ənd ˈðiː ˈkɛrfəli.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: OK. On Saturday, I bought a book and a notebook.
dialogue.reading: oʊˈkeɪ. ɑːn ˈsætərdeɪ, aɪ ˈbɔːt ə ˈbʊk ənd ə ˈnoʊtbʊk.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Good. Now tell me more about the book.
dialogue.reading: ˈɡʊd. ˈnaʊ ˈtɛl miː ˈmɔːr əˈbaʊt ðə ˈbʊk.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: The book is about a cat. The cat lives in a café.
dialogue.reading: ðə ˈbʊk ɪz əˈbaʊt ə ˈkæt. ðə ˈkæt ˈlɪvz ɪn ə kæˈfeɪ.

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Perfect! When you say a noun for the first time, use "a" or "an". The second time, use "the".
dialogue.reading: ˈpɜːrfɪkt! wɛn juː ˈseɪ ə ˈnaʊn fər ðə ˈfɜːrst ˈtaɪm, ˈjuːz ˈeɪ ɔːr ˈæn. ðə ˈsɛkənd ˈtaɪm, ˈjuːz ˈðiː.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: What about adjectives? Do I say "a old book"?
dialogue.reading: ˈwʌt əˈbaʊt ˈædʒɪktɪvz? duː aɪ ˈseɪ ˈeɪ ˈoʊld ˈbʊk?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: No, "an old book". We use "an" before a vowel sound.
dialogue.reading: ˈnoʊ, ˈæn ˈoʊld ˈbʊk. wiː ˈjuːz ˈæn bɪˈfɔːr ə ˈvaʊəl ˌsaʊnd.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: I see. And in the sentence "I like the book", is "like" a verb?
dialogue.reading: aɪ ˈsiː. ənd ɪn ðə ˈsɛntəns aɪ ˈlaɪk ðə ˈbʊk, ɪz ˈlaɪk ə ˈvɜːrb?

dialogue.speaker: b
dialogue.text: Yes. And "the" is an article. "A" and "an" are articles, too.
dialogue.reading: ˈjɛs. ənd ˈðiː ɪz ən ˈɑːrtɪkəl. ˈeɪ ənd ˈæn ər ˈɑːrtɪkəlz, ˈtuː.

dialogue.speaker: a
dialogue.text: Articles are hard for me. We don't have them in Thai!
dialogue.reading: ˈɑːrtɪkəlz ər ˈhɑːrd fər miː. wiː ˈdoʊnt ˈhæv ðɛm ɪn ˈtaɪ!
